All seeded data was removed and both quotations were restored from snapshot.

minor.issue: Reconciling a txn that is not paid sets payment_status='reconciled' and adds the sid to credited_sessions, but does not expire the Checkout Session in Stripe. If the client later pays that still-open session, verify_session marks it paid, and apply_payment_to_quotation finds the sid already in credited_sessions, returns False ('ya acreditada') and marks applied:true. The real charge is then silently absorbed: no credit, no needs_review, no duplicate warning.

The update has no atomic guard (the filter does not include applied != true); the guard is only a read in the route beforehand. A concurrent test (4 parallel POSTs) gave 1x200 and 3x400 with one audit entry, so it is fine in practice. Adding {'applied': {'$ne': True}} to the update_one filter and checking modified_count would make it race-proof.

A txn that was pending and then reconciled manually returns state 'paid' to the client, even though no card charge exists for that session. Low impact (only shown if the client comes back via the success_url).

issues: Sticky total/payment card overlaps the room-option list below it (e.g. the 'Triple' row is partly hidden behind the card at 1920x1080). Pre-existing, minor.

action_items: Optional hardening: on reconcile-manual of a non-paid txn, try stripe_expire_session first. Alternatively, if a txn with review_state 'manual' / payment_status 'reconciled' later becomes paid in Stripe, flag it needs_review or duplicate_warning instead of absorbing it silently through credited_sessions.
Optional: add an applied != true filter to the reconcile_manually update_one (atomic) and only write the audit entry when modified_count == 1.
critical_code_review_comments: public_payments.py is 728 lines (over 700); consider splitting the executive endpoints (verify-stripe, reconcile-manual, mark-paid) into their own router.
A fully paid quotation that also has a needs_review txn returns 409 with the needs_review message (instead of 400 'ya está pagada'). This seems intentional and is acceptable.

The verify-stripe duplicate detection falls back to local payment_status when the Stripe read fails. Correct as designed, but a txn reconciled manually from pending (payment_status 'reconciled') is never counted, even if Stripe actually shows it paid while reads fail.
